scope: Separate Japanese geometry prerequisite; unchanged EN-SW/ES corpus arm. No translation/reading/lemma/sense/POS/model acquisition.
raw: Whole unchanged text NLTokenizer.word with explicit Japanese locale, including attributes and original ranges.
projection: Protected intervals copied whole; each unchanged nonliteral region separately NLTokenizer.word tokenized and original offsets restored. Exact gaps become punctuation/symbol/other or separators. Native region geometry may differ from whole-text geometry; both retained. Projected native surfaces are classified by Unicode letters/digits, whitespace, punctuation and symbols; the NL word callback does not by itself make emoji or currency a word. Adjacent native ranges are coalesced only when their shared boundary cuts a single original grapheme; raw whole-text native ranges remain unchanged.
offsets: Half-open original Unicode scalar/codepoint and UTF16 offsets. No normalization. Grapheme alignment separately recorded.
reconstruction: Sorted tokens+separators cover original exactly once; whitespace internal to code remains in its literal. No partial protected overlap.
literal_policy: Code/Latin email/handle/number/Latin separator or alphanumeric identifier; supported ASCII URI. Broad non-ASCII URI bodies conservatively protected and diagnosed as boundary ambiguous, including undelimited Japanese suffixes. Not a general URI/Markdown parser.
evidence_limits: Retained authored/provider diagnostics, not new human conversational or population coverage.
Native geometry and exact reconstruction do not prove linguistic alignment or meanings.
Oversize input retained as an explicit rejected row, not a successful partition.

revision.reason: R01 reconstructed all accepted inputs but classified emoji/currency/isolated combining marks as words and split the NFD name José. Generic Unicode classification and grapheme-boundary-only coalescing; no phrase-specific overrides.
